title: Check where spacing rules put questions
statement: When a rule spaces a film's questions apart, check which placements it leaves: a rule that bars neighbouring parts can leave a short film only one.
example: With three parts, all five films one engine made stopped after their first and last parts, the second stop 0.5 s before the end.
detail: Both film blocks in the lesson engine enforce spacing in code: the film check wants stops at least 20 seconds apart, and the video essay wants its two questions after parts that are not next to each other (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/film-check.js`, `g9/transformer/src/mechanics/video-essay.js`). With three parts the second rule leaves a single placement, so each of the five films the engine made stopped after its first and last parts, never after the middle one, and each second question came 0.5 s before the film ended (stops and durations in each film's `manifest.json` under `g9-transformer-runs/films/`). One of them, recorded in the engine's QA, ran 36.8 s with stops at 10.82 s and 36.26 s.
against: No source gives a reason for either rule; the video tool's handoff only restates the first: "That mechanic requires two to four stops spaced at least 20 seconds apart" (g9/tools/unit-video-essay/HANDOFF.md line 31). A four-part film would leave three placements.

evidence.quote: check("checks-apart", "The checks follow different beats, not one after the other",
check("spaced", "Stops at least 20 seconds apart", gaps.every((g) => g >= 20), "two stops are less than 20 seconds apart"),
Film `7fc2d6f7b8e85a6b`: 36.8 s, stops at 10.82 s and 36.26 s.
